subject: Human Evolution
title: Insect Eating
description: A short lesson to help you apply Insect Eating.

hook.text: A termite mound holds millions of protein-rich insects. Chimps fish for them with twigs—and so did we.

buildup.text: Insects are calorie-dense, abundant, and available year-round in tropical and subtropical zones.

discovery.text: Entomophagy—insect eating—was likely a staple for early hominins, not a last-resort food.

twist.text: Western disgust at insects is cultural, not biological. Two billion people still eat them regularly.

climax.text: Insects may have bridged the gap between a fruit diet and a meat diet in hominin evolution.

punchline.text: Bugs were our first protein supplement.

quiz.question: What role did insects likely play in early hominin diets?
options: A reliable protein source bridging fruit and meat diets
